Aside from taste, I'd like to know what addatives give you specific feelings.

The very cold on inhale feeling.

The horseradish/wasabi nose exhale.

The pinpoint heat of extremely spicy hot sauce.

The tongue numbness of pineapple.

The tongue tingle of sodapop/poprocks/champaign.

And I'm sure a bunch of other feelings (and not tastes/flavors)

Anyone know the specific addatives and % for these?
[Help] trying to figure out the feels.

Koolada is going to give you have cold, frozen kind of feeling. It's tasteless in and of itself, but it'll add a massive throat hit with a "cold" sensation - which is why it works so well with mints and fruits. Just about everyone sells Koolada.

Flavor West and LorAnn Oils both sell a 'sour' agent, that without flavor per se, will certainly add a definitive "Sour" pucker to anything you put it in.

TFA Smooth and Ethyl Maltol "dull" sharp flavors and add a bit of a "cottony" sensation in high enough amounts. Too much will make you feel like you're trying to breathe through a pillow.

Acetyl Pyrazine is everything that is "bread" without the specific bread, wheat, oat tastes. There is a bit of taste to it, but I notice the effects of a 'substance' addition, instead of a flavoring addition, when used with cookies, pies, donut - bakery type flavors.

I know there are flavor additives that add spiciness, like that of horseradish and wasabi, but I haven't ever tried any of them. Nor will I, to be honest.

I'm not sure if there's anything to add the tongue tingle of carbonated drinks - though that effect certainly would be cool to implement in certain mixes.

Though I can't speak for certainty on every additive ever put out there, I can speak of a few of them. Hopefully it was of some use to you.

I'm getting into Bitcoin (been lurking here) and was excitedly telling my wife what I had learned so far. She's Russian and also spent some time in Greece so she is interested in all the Bitcoin news coming out of Europe

I suggested we start using Bitcoin. She asked if we could use it to buy groceries at our local supermarket. Umm, no. Can we get gas or pay the hydro bill with it? Well, not really. Can we use it downtown or at the mall? Unfortunately no.

Then she asked "So what's the point of having Bitcoin?" I realized she wanted practical, everyday uses for it and I couldn't think of a single one!

Can you guys fill me in on how Bitcoin could improve my life over fiat money? We live in the Toronto area, Ontario, Canada and there's a couple of Bitcoin ATMs nearby. Aside from novelty use, why would I get Bitcoin?
Wife asked "What will we do with Bitcoin?" and I didn't have an answer.
Use it to save 20% - 30% on Amazon purchases with Purse.io. I've used it 3 or 4 times now and works great!
I believe if you get inventive with it you can almost buy anything. Regarding paying bills... here is a Canadian company that I found https://www.bylls.com/. I believe there are others too.

If you send money overseas and you can convince the other party to open up a Bitcoin exchange account on their end, then you can also save the fees that way. Not to mention it would likely be quicker even by the time you fund your account and the other party withdraws to their bank account.

At this point you would buy it because you think it might have a use in the future and be worth more than you payed for it now. In other words speculation. Day to day there isn't much use for it yet. Frictionless global money with an API is something that the world hasn't seen before so nobody knows what to do with it yet. ;)
You buy wealth no one can take away

As far as using it "downtown or at the mall" install Gyft or eGifter and you can buy discounted giftcards with bitcoin while you wait for your meal or are in line at the register. I've done this a number of times and it works great and saves money due to the points, and sometimes direct discounts, you get through these apps.
You can buy cool stuff from fasttech.com without giving money to paypal.

Tell your wife that Bitcoin is a long term investment. You can keep up with your country's politics and economic events but you will never truly know when disaster will strike and will no longer have access to your hard earned savings. Bitcoin is proof that we can have a medium of exchange without the help of a centralized authority. All that is left to do now is educate others about it and use it where you can as a currency.
